Workflow for small language model fine-tuning

From base model to domain-specific small language model, stage by stage.

This is the product path from custom dataset ingestion to training, evaluation, export, and deployment. In the app it is four places in a project's sidebar — Data, Train, Results, Ship — with an Overview that says where you are and what the next step is. Every stage has explicit inputs and outputs, and the stages that write to the audit log say so below, so ML engineers can see exactly what happened to their base model and their data.

The workspace

Six destinations, one project

Every project opens on its Overview: the current stage, one button for the next step, the latest run's lift against its base model, the shipped export, and up to three Coach notices worth a look. The sidebar below it is the whole map: Data (five steps: Sources, Prepare, Labels, Generate, Split), Train (one form), Results (Verdict, Failures, Compare, Try it), Ship (Package, Publish, Deploy, Monitor) and Settings. Quick search (⌘K / Ctrl+K) jumps to any of them.

Lifecycle map

The pipeline, stage by stage

01

Sources

Where: Data → Sources. Upload files, Import dataset (auto-mapping), or No documents yet? Write sample documents.

Inputs: a browser upload, or a source locator (jsonl:/path, file:/path, hf:id:split, kaggle:competition:slug, git:<url>[@ref], web:<seed url>).

Outputs: rows on disk in the project's data dir.

Contract: source connectors implement load() + describe(). Unparseable rows surface as sentinel rows, not silent drops. A file that cannot be parsed is an error, never accepted text.

RunEvent: a document upload emits ingestion / info; a dataset import emits one when it runs (next stage).

02

Introspect & map

Where: the import wizard behind Import dataset: Source → Task type → Map → Preview & Confirm.

Inputs: ~20 sample rows from the source; then locator + mapper + field map + optional drop reasons.

Outputs: ranked ShapeHypothesis list + a top ProposedMapping with confidence + rationale; on confirm, rows appended to the project's synthetic JSONL, written as accepted: imported rows skip the review queue and train directly, so the preview is the review.

Contract: never silently auto-picks — below 0.80 the UI asks you to confirm you reviewed the proposal (CLI: --force). Per-row accountability: every row is a TransformedRow or a RejectedRow with a stable reason code; rejected rows are grouped by reason and bulk-droppable, and the counts stay in the audit row.

RunEvent: ingestion / dataset_import_run on success, dataset_import_failed on error, from the run only (introspect and preview write none). Payload: source, mapper, accepted/rejected counts, written_path, config_id.

03

Prepare

Where: Data → Prepare — chunk size, redact PII & secrets, Clean All Documents.

Inputs: the project's RawDocuments.

Outputs: cleaned text + chunks JSONL + per-document metadata (PII findings, quality score, text hash). Row files are cleaned row by row; only documents are chunked, on sentence boundaries.

Contract: runs as a background task that the notification bell follows, so the HTTP request never blocks.

RunEvent: none today. The taxonomy declares cleaning codes, but the clean step does not emit them yet; the notification bell reports the background task.

04

Labels

Where: Data → Labels — confirm the task shape ("What kind of task is this?") and build the answer key, the held-out set every score is measured against.

Inputs: your own labelled rows, rows drafted by a model and checked by a person, or (for span projects) labelling conventions, one line per type.

Outputs: a confirmed task profile + adapter preset that split, train and eval all read; the answer key (practice / final), kept out of training.

Contract: a leaked answer key makes a score measure memorisation, so train↔answer-key overlap is scanned and flagged.

RunEvent: none — labelling is data, not a run.

05

Generate

Where: Data → Generate — synthetic data: Single-turn Q&A, Multi-turn, or PII / NER span extraction; provider (local Ollama first, or a cloud model); playbooks matched to the task shape.

Inputs: cleaned passages (or pasted source text) + a generation model.

Outputs: rows in the project's synthetic JSONL, pending until accepted in the review queue (in the step's Details drawer).

Contract: pending and rejected rows never train. Offsets on span rows are verified against the text, never trusted. A batch that validates to nothing yields nothing and says why.

RunEvent: a background Job per batch; the bell reports rows kept and the diagnostic when none were.

06

Split

Where: Data → Split — train / validation / test, the dataset adapter, dedup, and Keep the current test examples on every later split.

Inputs: cleaned + accepted synthetic rows; the project's dataset-adapter preset.

Outputs: prepared/manifest.json + train.jsonl / val.jsonl / test.jsonl, plus a versioned snapshot of each split. Carries task_profile + output_schema.scoring_mode.

Contract: the manifest is the record of the split (row counts, task profile, scoring mode, file hashes); training reads the split files themselves. Keeping the test examples means a new run is scored on the same rows as the last one.

RunEvent: none; the manifest and the split snapshot are the record.

07

Train

Where: Train — one form: base model (+ Browse), task, one run or three seeds, run name, a readiness line, and Train. Epochs, LoRA, checks, cloud burst, presets and the plan-vs-data gaps wait under More options. The runs list with each run's live dashboard sits below the form.

Inputs: prepared manifest + base model + the resolved config (shown in a confirm dialog with an estimate before Launch).

Outputs: checkpoints + per-step loss / eval traces + adapter weights (or a full model for encoders). Preflight runs first and returns errors and warnings: an error blocks the launch, a warning does not (the readiness line on the form shows both).

Contract: preflight → a training job queued to the Celery worker (Redis plus a worker are required with the default TRAINING_BACKEND=external) → checkpoints → when a real run completes, a post_training_lift_eval Job scores the base model and the run on the same test split. Tokenizing and loss masking happen in the trainer. Cancel stops the process.

RunEvent: training / info when a run starts (payload: experiment_id, runtime_id, base_model, training_mode, epochs, total_steps). training_dispatch_error when the job cannot be queued. Simulate runs also write a completion event, or training_runtime_error. A real run that fails later (a crash, a non-zero exit, a timeout) is marked failed on the run but writes no timeline event today. Fix coming: a change that records why a real run failed, puts it on the timeline and offers to continue from the last checkpoint is merged but not yet released.

08

Results

Where: Results — Verdict (did it work? the lift against the base model, pass/fail rules, the scorecard), Failures (where it fails: clusters, eval gaps, built-in and custom checks, slices), Compare (other runs, external benchmarks, Auto-RAG) and Try it (chat with the run; a redaction box for span runs).

Inputs: trained model + the test examples (or the answer key) + the rule set.

Outputs: task-aware metrics (per-class P/R/F1, span-set, faithfulness, alignment margin, BLEU/ROUGE, WER, etc.), paired base-vs-fine-tuned evidence (better / worse / within noise), and the pass/fail verdict.

Contract: the task-handler dispatcher picks the scorer from the task profile: ClassificationHandler, QAHandler, StructuredExtractionHandler (span_set or field_match), RAGHandler, AlignmentHandler, Seq2SeqHandler, VisionLanguageHandler, AudioTranscriptHandler, SafetyHandler or ToolCallHandler, with GenericHandler as the fallback. The metric shape comes from the handler's score(); the pass/fail rules in the rule set decide the verdict. They block an export only when the project's gate policy says so, which is off by default. The lift check runs by itself when a real run completes (not for simulate or weightless runs; turn it off with auto_lift_eval=false).

RunEvent: eval / info when an eval completes, parented to exp-<id> (payload: eval_type, dataset_name, pass_rate). The taxonomy's eval_* failure codes are not emitted yet.

09

Package & publish

Where: Ship → Package (New export: run, format, quantization, deployment targets; the Releases table; Options: Compress and the manifest) and Ship → Publish (a completed Hugging Face export to the Hub).

Inputs: trained model + target format (Hugging Face / GGUF / ONNX / TensorRT / Docker). vLLM is a deployment target under Ship → Deploy, not an export format.

Outputs: artifact bundle with weights, tokenizer, manifest, smoke-check trace. A LoRA run is merged first.

Contract: quantization variants (Q4_K_M, AWQ, GPTQ) are tracked per run so a GGUF export packages only that run's compressed files — no raw-weights fallback under a compressed label.

RunEvent: export / info on success (payload: format, output_path, file_size_bytes); export_run_failed when an export fails. An export blocked by the gate policy is marked failed without an event.

10

Deploy & monitor (optional)

Where: Ship → Deploy (serve / deploy plans, served versions) and Ship → Monitor (run events, failure clusters, drift).

Inputs: an export + a target (vLLM endpoint / local runner / cloud burst).

Outputs: a versioned DeploymentVersion with promote / reject / rollback / drift-check actions.

Contract: smoke checks run at export time; promote marks a pending version live and supersedes the previous one. The drift check runs on demand: it scores the answer key by exact match, from predictions you post or from a live endpoint, and compares the pass rate with the latest eval of the run the export came from; a change of more than 0.05 (the default tolerance) flags drift.

RunEvent: deployment / info per action (record, promote, reject, rollback).

What each stage records and enforces today

The audit-log taxonomy declares 35 reason codes; the public code emits 9 of them today. This table lists only what the released code does. Sources: the emit_event() call sites and models/reason_codes.py in the BrewSLM backend; the gate check in services/export_service.py.

Stage Emitted to the audit log today Applied or enforced today Declared, not emitted yet
01 Sourcesingestion / info per uploaded documentA file that cannot be parsed is an error, never accepted textingest_io_error, ingest_unsupported_format, ingest_validation_failed
02 Introspect & mapdataset_import_run (info) or dataset_import_failed (error), from the run onlyThe 0.80 confidence gate; imported rows are written as accepted and skip the review queue—
03 PrepareNothing (a background Job the bell follows)—cleaning_pii_block, cleaning_outlier_threshold_exceeded
04 LabelsLabelling jobs: annotation_job_created, annotation_label_submitted, annotation_rows_promoted (info)The answer key is kept out of training—
05 GenerateNothing (a background Job per batch)Pending and rejected rows never train—
06 SplitNothing; the manifest and the split snapshot are the recordKeep the current test examples, when you ask for itadapter_field_resolution_failed, adapter_schema_mismatch
07 TrainStart (info); training_dispatch_error; simulate runs: completion or training_runtime_error; distillation_teacher_capture (info) when teacher logits are capturedPreflight errors block the launch; warnings do nottraining_oom, training_timeout, training_cancelled (and training_runtime_error for real runs)
08 Resultseval / info per completed evalThe pass/fail verdict is shown on Verdict; on its own it blocks nothingeval_dataset_missing, eval_judge_unavailable, eval_runtime_error
09 Packageexport / info, or export_run_failedRequired rules block an export only when the project's gate policy is set (off by default)export_artifact_missing, export_quantization_failed
10 Deploy & monitordeployment / info per actionThe drift check runs on demand, by exact match, tolerance 0.05deployment_drift_detected, deployment_promote_blocked, deployment_rollback_no_predecessor, deployment_smoke_failed

Also declared and not emitted: the autopilot_*, extension_* and system_* codes. The full list, code by code, is in Lesson 3.12, the RunEvent and Coach catalogue.

Two screens

Train is a form; Results is a verdict

Audit spine

One stream powers everything observability-related

Producers

Document uploads, imports, annotation, teacher-logit capture, training (starts and dispatch errors), eval, export and deployment write RunEvent rows via emit_event(); the table above says which. Severity is one of info / warning / error / critical, and an error or critical row must carry a reason code from the taxonomy or it is rejected. The taxonomy declares more codes than the stages emit today.

Consumers

The run timeline and the failure-cluster surface on Ship → Monitor, and the support bundle. (Background Jobs are a separate stream: the notification bell follows anything still running.)

Why this matters

Adding a new pipeline stage is just: pick a stage constant, register a reason code, emit an event. Every downstream view picks it up automatically. A stage that emits nothing (Prepare, Labels, Split, preflight today) leaves no trace there, which is why the table above says what is emitted today rather than what the taxonomy declares.

Best-effort hooks: the audit emission is wrapped in try/except at every call site. A bug in observability cannot break the data write path.

Learn The Concept

The Academy lessons behind the workflow

BrewSLM automates the lifecycle, but the underlying ideas still matter when you choose a base model, build a gold set (the answer key under Data → Labels), or decide whether a training run actually improved the model.

Training loop

Understand what the platform is doing when it tokenizes, computes loss, steps the optimizer, and saves checkpoints.

  • The training loop, step by step
  • Read the logs, loss, and checkpoints

Evaluation and gates

Promotion gates only make sense if they are anchored to the right metric and a held-out gold set. In BrewSLM they are the pass/fail rules on Results → Verdict.

  • Gold sets
  • Evaluation that matches the task

Serving and rerouting

Know when to ship the fine-tuned model, when to quantize it, and when retrieval is the better answer.

  • Serving and inference optimization
  • When not to fine-tune: auto-RAG and reroute

Try the path end-to-end

One command per stage. No glue scripts.

# ingest + map via the generic pipeline (imdb maps to classification)

$ python -m app.cli.dataset_import run \

    --locator hf:imdb:train --project 1 --auto --limit 5000

 

# or, in the workspace:

# Data → Sources → "Import dataset (auto-mapping)"

 

# train from the Train page: base model, task, seeds → Train

 

# or, scripted:

$ curl -X POST localhost:8000/api/projects/1/training/experiments \

    -H 'X-API-Key: sk-mock-admin-key' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \

    -d '{"name": "first-run", "config": {"base_model": "HuggingFaceTB/SmolLM2-135M-Instruct"}}'

$ curl -X POST -H 'X-API-Key: sk-mock-admin-key' \

    localhost:8000/api/projects/1/training/experiments/<id>/start
